title: Enable nonRoot feature gate in OCPvirt prior to 4.18
description: Root is a default account with elevated privileges, including full administrative access to both security and non - security related functions. The "nonRoot" feature gate in OpenShift environments ensures virtual machine access is restricted to resources and functionality required to operate. Audit: Passes when .spec.featureGates.nonRoot of the HyperConverged resource is true, or when the cluster is OpenShift 4.18 or newer where the setting is ignored and always enabled. Requires oc logged in to the cluster with read access.
reference: CIS Red Hat OpenShift Virtual Machine Extension Benchmark v1.0.0 - 1.2 Enable nonRoot feature gate in OCPvirt prior to 4.18

audit.command: command -v oc >/dev/null 2>&1 || exit 1; v=$(oc get hyperconverged kubevirt-hyperconverged -n openshift-cnv -o jsonpath='{.spec.featureGates.nonRoot}') || exit 1; mi=$(oc get clusterversion version -o jsonpath='{.status.desired.version}' 2>/dev/null | cut -d. -f2); if [ "$v" = true ] || { [ -n "$mi" ] && [ "$mi" -ge 18 ] 2>/dev/null; }; then echo compliant; else echo noncompliant; fi

remediation.command: Enable nonRoot and set its value to True . $ oc patch hyperconverged kubevirt-hyperconverged - n openshift - cnv --type='json' -p='[ {"op": "replace", "path": "/spec/featureGates/nonRoot", "value": true }, ]'

title: Enforce the use of trusted registries using TLS
description: Transport Layer Security (TLS) is a cryptographic protocol used in this context to protect data in transit. Restricting operations to the use of trusted registries ensures the use of approved container images. Audit: Passes when .spec.storageImport.insecureRegistries of the HyperConverged resource is empty. Requires oc logged in to the cluster with read access.
reference: CIS Red Hat OpenShift Virtual Machine Extension Benchmark v1.0.0 - 1.5 Enforce the use of trusted registries using TLS

audit.command: command -v oc >/dev/null 2>&1 || exit 1; v=$(oc get hyperconverged kubevirt-hyperconverged -n openshift-cnv -o jsonpath='{.spec.storageImport.insecureRegistries}') || exit 1; [ -z "$v" ] && echo compliant || echo noncompliant

remediation.command: Do not allow connections to insecure registries from hyperconverged resources. The cluster administrator can remove any insecure registry: $ oc patch hyperconverged kubevirt-hyperconverged - n openshift - cnv --type='json' -p='[ {"op": "remove", "path": "/spec/storageImport/insecureRegistries"}, ]'

title: Restrict GPU and USB pass through to approved devices
description: The ability to pass through devices provides the capability to offload tasks from the CPU to the device itself. The benchmark marks this recommendation Manual; TMAegis reports it as a manual review item with the audit steps.
reference: CIS Red Hat OpenShift Virtual Machine Extension Benchmark v1.0.0 - 1.1 Restrict GPU and USB pass through to approved devices

audit.command: List the host devices available to virtualization workloads and verify the host devices returned are necessary for workload execution. $ oc get hyperconverged kubevirt - hyperconverged - n openshift - cnv -ojsonpath='{.spec.permittedHostDevices}'

remediation.command: Enforcing limitations to the passthroughof approved devices protects against the introduction of a malicious or unknown device to the system. The system administrator can remove the unwanted devices by patching the HCO object. { "mediatedDevices": [ { "mdevNameSelector": "DEVICE_A", "resourceName": "vendor.com/DEVICE_A" } ], "pciHostDevices": [ { "externalResourceProvider": true, "pciDeviceSelector": "XXX:YYY", "resourceName": "vendor.com/DEVICE_B" }, { "pciDeviceSelector": "NNN:MMM", "resourceName": "vendor.com/DEVICE_C" } ], "usbHostDevices": [ { "resourceName": "kubevirt.io/storage", "selectors": [ { "product": "0001", "vendor": "46f4" } ] } ] If the first PCI device (the DEVICE_A at index 0, in bold) should not be permitted to be passed through to a VM, here’s how to remove it: $ oc ...

title: Disable persistentReservations feature gate
description: Persistentreservations are used to reserve a shared LUN among multiple virtual machines. This feature is required when the Windows guest makes use of the Windows Shared Cluster Filesystem. Enabling persistent reservations introduces additional complexity and overhead, as it requires calculated management of resource allocation and monitoring to ensure that reservations are not overcommitted and do not impact the overall performance of the system. Enabling the persistent reservations feature introduces and relies upon an optional component with elevated privileges (qemu - pr - helper). ... Audit: Passes when .spec.featureGates.persistentReservation is false or unset (the default is disabled). Requires oc logged in to the cluster with read access.
reference: CIS Red Hat OpenShift Virtual Machine Extension Benchmark v1.0.0 - 1.3 Disable persistentReservations feature gate

audit.command: command -v oc >/dev/null 2>&1 || exit 1; v=$(oc get hyperconverged kubevirt-hyperconverged -n openshift-cnv -o jsonpath='{.spec.featureGates.persistentReservation}') || exit 1; [ "$v" = true ] && echo noncompliant || echo compliant

remediation.command: Disable the persistent reservations feature by setting to persistentReservations False for applicable hyperconverged resources. $ oc patch hyperconverged kubevirt - hyperconverged - n openshift - cnv -- type='json' -p='[ {"op": "replace", "path": "/spec/featureGates/persistentReservation", "value": false }, ]'

title: Disable downwardMetrics feature gate
description: The downwardMetrics feature allows users to collect and monitor additional metrics related to host and virtual machine performance. Audit: Passes when .spec.featureGates.downwardMetrics is false or unset (the default is disabled). Requires oc logged in to the cluster with read access.
reference: CIS Red Hat OpenShift Virtual Machine Extension Benchmark v1.0.0 - 1.4 Disable downwardMetrics feature gate

audit.command: command -v oc >/dev/null 2>&1 || exit 1; v=$(oc get hyperconverged kubevirt-hyperconverged -n openshift-cnv -o jsonpath='{.spec.featureGates.downwardMetrics}') || exit 1; [ "$v" = true ] && echo noncompliant || echo compliant

remediation.command: Set downwardMetrics to False $ oc patch hyperconverged kubevirt-hyperconverged - n openshift - cnv --type='json' -p='[ {"op": "replace", "path": "/spec/featureGates/downwardMetrics", "value": false }, ]'

title: Restrict patching operations in the annotations for Hyperconverged
description: The kubevirt - hyperconverged (HCO) object provides a mechanism to customize OpenShift Virtualization components through the control of patching operations. Although this approach itself does not inherently introduce security risks, enabling experimental features may have unintended consequences and might not be officially supported. It is essential to weigh the benefits of using these options against any potential security implications before proceeding. The benchmark marks this recommendation Manual; TMAegis reports it as a manual review item with the audit steps.
reference: CIS Red Hat OpenShift Virtual Machine Extension Benchmark v1.0.0 - 1.6 Restrict patching operations in the annotations for Hyperconverged

audit.command: Ensure there are no patching operations for the Openshift Virtualization component $ oc get hyperconverged kubevirt - hyperconverged - n openshift - cnv - o jsonpath='{.metadata.annotations}'| jq '.|has("kubevirt.kubevirt.io/jsonpatch")' $ oc get hyperconverged kubevirt-hyperconverged -n openshift-cnv -o jsonpath='{.metadata.annotations}'| jq '.|has("containerizeddataimporter.kubevirt.io/jsonpatch")' $ oc get hyperconverged kubevirt-hyperconverged -n openshift-cnv -o jsonpath='{.metadata.annotations}'| jq '.|has("networkaddonsconfigs.kubevirt.io/jsonpatch")' $ oc get hyperconverged kubevirt-hyperconverged -n openshift-cnv -o jsonpath='{.metadata.annotations}'| jq ...

remediation.command: The annotations should be removed from the Hyperconverged. For example, by directly editing the object with oc edit hyperconverged kubevirt - hyperconverged -n openshift-cnv or by removing the annotation with the annotate command. Example: $ oc annotate --overwrite -n openshift-cnv hco kubevirt-hyperconverged 'containerizeddataimporter.kubevirt.io/jsonpatch-'

title: Ensure kubevirt seccomp profile file permission is set to 700 or more restrictive
description: Setting the kubevirt Secure Computing Mode (seccomp) file permissions to 700 or more restrictive limits access to security related administrative functionality to approved administrators. Audit: Passes when the seccomp profile file of every virt-handler pod is mode 700 or more restrictive; a pod where the file does not exist (Secure Computing Mode feature gate not enabled) is not applicable. Requires oc logged in to the cluster with read access.
reference: CIS Red Hat OpenShift Virtual Machine Extension Benchmark v1.0.0 - 1.8 Ensure kubevirt seccomp profile file permission is set to 700 or more restrictive

audit.command: command -v oc >/dev/null 2>&1 || exit 1; bad=0; n=0; for pod in $(oc get pod -n openshift-cnv -l kubevirt.io=virt-handler --no-headers -o custom-columns=":metadata.name" 2>/dev/null); do n=$((n+1)); m=$(oc exec -n openshift-cnv "$pod" -c virt-handler -- sh -c 'f=/proc/1/root/var/lib/kubelet/seccomp/kubevirt/kubevirt.json; [ -e "$f" ] && stat -c %a "$f" || echo absent' 2>/dev/null); case "$m" in absent) ;; [0-7][0-7][0-7]|[0-7][0-7][0-7][0-7]) [ $((8#$m & 8#077)) -eq 0 ] || bad=1;; *) bad=1;; esac; done; [ "$n" -gt 0 ] || exit 1; [ "$bad" -eq 0 ] && echo compliant || echo noncompliant

remediation.command: Update the permissions on each node using chmod : $ oc exec <virt-handler-pod> -ti -n openshift-cnv -- chmod 700 /proc/1/root/var/lib/kubelet/seccomp/kubevirt/kubevirt.json

title: Ensure kubevirt cache directory permission is set to 755 or more restrictive
description: Setting the kubevirt private directory to 755 or more restrictive limits access to security related administrative functionality to approved administrators. Audit: Passes when /var/run/kubevirt-private in every virt-handler pod is mode 755 or more restrictive; a pod where the directory does not exist is not applicable. Requires oc logged in to the cluster with read access.
reference: CIS Red Hat OpenShift Virtual Machine Extension Benchmark v1.0.0 - 1.9 Ensure kubevirt cache directory permission is set to 755 or more restrictive

audit.command: command -v oc >/dev/null 2>&1 || exit 1; bad=0; n=0; for pod in $(oc get pod -n openshift-cnv -l kubevirt.io=virt-handler --no-headers -o custom-columns=":metadata.name" 2>/dev/null); do n=$((n+1)); m=$(oc exec -n openshift-cnv "$pod" -- sh -c '[ -e /var/run/kubevirt-private ] && stat -c %a /var/run/kubevirt-private || echo absent' 2>/dev/null); case "$m" in absent) ;; [0-7][0-7][0-7]|[0-7][0-7][0-7][0-7]) [ $((8#$m & ~8#755 & 8#7777)) -eq 0 ] || bad=1;; *) bad=1;; esac; done; [ "$n" -gt 0 ] || exit 1; [ "$bad" -eq 0 ] && echo compliant || echo noncompliant

remediation.command: Update the permissions on each virt-handller using : chmod $ oc exec <virt-handler-pod> -ti -n openshift-cnv -- chmod 755 /var/run/kubevirt-private

title: Restrict namespace administrator access to migration tools
description: Namespace administrators have the capability to perform live migrations, which can potentially impact other users of the system. Live migration is a process where virtual machines can be moved from one physical host to another without any downtime, making it a valuable tool for managing clusters and ensuring high availability. However, since live migration involves moving data between hosts, it can have an impact on other users who may have applications running on the same hosts. As such, it is important to exercise caution when granting access to namespace administrators and ensure that appropriate safeguards are in place to minimize any potential disruptions. The benchmark marks this recommendation Manual; TMAegis reports it as a manual review item with the audit steps.
reference: CIS Red Hat OpenShift Virtual Machine Extension Benchmark v1.0.0 - 1.10 Restrict namespace administrator access to migration tools

audit.command: Use the following command to find users, service accounts and groups who are allowed to create VirtualMachineInterfaceMigration and MigrationPolicy resources: $ oc adm policy who - can create vmim $ oc adm policy who - can create migrationpolicy Ensure users are authorized to perform those actions.

remediation.command: Remove access to virtualmachineinstancemigration and migrationpolicy objects create in the cluster. Example: Remove create access given by the clusterRoleBinding for the I migrationpolicy for the test user # Get all the users and service accounts who can create migrationpolicies $ oc adm policy who-can create migrationpolicy Users: system:admin .. Test # Verify that the test user can create the migrationpolicy $ oc auth can-i create migrationpolicies --as test Warning: resource 'migrationpolicies' is not namespace scoped in group 'migrations.kubevirt.io' yes # Find out which rolebinding or clusterrolbinding associated to the test user $ oc get rolebindings,clusterrolebindings --all-namespaces -o custom-columns='KIND:kind,NAMESPACE:metadata.namespace,NAME:metadata.n ...

title: Restrict exec access to the pods
description: The ability to exec commands in a pod allows for arbitrary execution by users. This includes administrative functions which normally require elevation of privileges by an approved administrator, and could lead to unauthorized use of both security and non - security related administrative functions. The benchmark marks this recommendation Manual; TMAegis reports it as a manual review item with the audit steps.
reference: CIS Red Hat OpenShift Virtual Machine Extension Benchmark v1.0.0 - 1.11 Restrict exec access to the pods

audit.command: To verify who can exec commands in pods, use the following command: $ oc adm policy who - can exec pod

remediation.command: Assign exec access to pods in the cluster only to approved administrators.

title: Restrict VNC access to cluster workloads
description: Access to each workload’s virtual screen is provided via VNC. Permission to use VNC is granted via a role, which means users with role assigned can access the VNC console of all workloads in a namespace. The benchmark marks this recommendation Manual; TMAegis reports it as a manual review item with the audit steps.
reference: CIS Red Hat OpenShift Virtual Machine Extension Benchmark v1.0.0 - 1.12 Restrict VNC access to cluster workloads

audit.command: Verify to which users have the necessary permissions to create tokens: $ oc get rolebinding - ojson | jq - c '.items[] | select(.roleRef.name | contains("token.kubevirt.io:generate"))'

remediation.command: Assign this RoleBinding only to users with approval to use it, otherwise remove unapproved users.

title: Restrict access to create and modify the Virtual Machine Cluster Instance and Preference Types
description: An instance type is a reusable object used to create VMs with sane defaults based on the desired type of VM. Since the object is used to create instances of VMs in the entire cluster, its creation and update needs to be carefully and securely managed. The benchmark marks this recommendation Manual; TMAegis reports it as a manual review item with the audit steps.
reference: CIS Red Hat OpenShift Virtual Machine Extension Benchmark v1.0.0 - 1.13 Restrict access to create and modify the Virtual Machine Cluster Instance and Preference Types

audit.command: Check who has the ability to create InstanceTypes with the following command: $ oc adm policy who - can create,update virtualmachineclusterinstancetypes

remediation.command: Assign create and update access only to approved virtualmachineclusterinstancetypes objects in the cluster. Remove the create and update permission from users who are not authorized to perform the actions.

title: Restrict update access to the CDI CR
description: The CDI object is not namespaced and contains sensitive configuration data for the Containerized Data Importer. The benchmark marks this recommendation Manual; TMAegis reports it as a manual review item with the audit steps.
reference: CIS Red Hat OpenShift Virtual Machine Extension Benchmark v1.0.0 - 1.14 Restrict update access to the CDI CR

audit.command: check who can update the cdi resources: $ oc adm policy who - can update cdi

remediation.command: Assign update access only to approved cdi objects in the cluster.

title: Restrict pass through of GPUs and Host devices to the Virtual Machine
description: The ability to pass through certain devices like a GPU or NVMe can improve performance by offloading certain tasks from the CPU to the device itself, but it also introduces shared system resources and additional attack vectors for bad actors. Configuring GPUs or host devices for the virtual machine can put the guest at risk. It's important to be selective and only enable passthrough for devices that are critical to the operation of your workloads. The benchmark marks this recommendation Manual; TMAegis reports it as a manual review item with the audit steps.
reference: CIS Red Hat OpenShift Virtual Machine Extension Benchmark v1.0.0 - 2.1 Restrict pass through of GPUs and Host devices to the Virtual Machine

audit.command: Use the following command to list gpus associated with a virtual machine: $ oc get vm -A -ojson | jq '.items[] | select(.spec.template.spec.domain.devices.gpus | length > 0) | {vm_name: .metadata.name, namespace: .metadata.namespace, gpus: .spec.template.spec.domain.devices.gpus}' Use the following command to list hostDevices associated with a virtual machine: $ oc get vm -A -ojson | jq '.items[].spec.template.spec.domain.devices.hostDevices' This check applies to any created VMs. Results of this query will be in this form: [ { "deviceName": "<resource - name>", "name": "<device - name>" }, { "deviceName": "<resource - name>", "name": "<device - name>" } ]

remediation.command: Only enable approved devices which are trust - worthy and strictly necessary by the workload. For example, if the first host device above (index 0, in bold) should not be permitted to be passed through to a given VM, here’s how to remove it: $ oc patch vm <vm-name> --type='json' -p='[ {"op": "remove", "path": "/spec/template/spec/domain/devices/hostDevices/0"}, ]'

title: Disable overcommitting guest memory
description: The overcommitGuestOverhead configuration option enables the request for additional virtual machine management memory inside the virt - launcher pod. The overcommit feature is used to increase virtual machine density on the node, as long as the virtual machine doesn’t request all the memory that it would need if fully loaded. However, if the VM were to use all of the memory it could, this would lead to the OpenShift Scheduler killing the workload. The benchmark marks this recommendation Manual; TMAegis reports it as a manual review item with the audit steps.
reference: CIS Red Hat OpenShift Virtual Machine Extension Benchmark v1.0.0 - 2.2 Disable overcommitting guest memory

audit.command: Verify that no virtual machines are using the overcommitGuestOverhead setting: $ oc get vm - ojson - A |jq '.items[] | select(.spec.template.spec.domain.resources.overcommitGuestOverhead == true)| .metadata.namespace + "/" + .metadata.name'

remediation.command: Stop any guest with this flag enabled and remove the flag before restarting. This flag can be removed on a given VM with the following command: $ oc patch vm <vm-name> --type='json' -p='[ {"op": "remove", "path": "/spec/template/spec/domain/resources/overcommitGuestOverhead"}, ]'

title: Restrict access to cross datavolumes cloning
description: Datavolume cross-namespace cloning allows cloning a datavolume from one namespace to another, breaking the namespace isolation. The benchmark marks this recommendation Manual; TMAegis reports it as a manual review item with the audit steps.
reference: CIS Red Hat OpenShift Virtual Machine Extension Benchmark v1.0.0 - 3.1 Restrict access to cross datavolumes cloning

audit.command: To check which role bindings have the ability to clone across namespaces, use the following command where to list all the rolebinding and verify which one has a ClusterRole which enables it to operate on data volumes and have bound a service account in another namespace . Ensure that the destination namespace is a desired one. $ oc get rolebinding - n <source - namespace> <allow - clone - to - user> - oyaml Output will be in the following format: apiVersion: rbac.authorization.k8s.io/v1 kind: RoleBinding metadata: name: <role - binding - name> namespace: <source namespace> subjects: - kind: ServiceAccount name: default namespace: <destination namespace> roleRef: kind: ClusterRole name: ...

remediation.command: Remove any rolebinding resources that grant unintended access across namespaces. Please refer to the latest OpenShift documentation for details on this process.

title: Disable Shareable disks
description: Sharable disks are shared between VMs, and they can be used only if a filesystem installed on top of it is a cluster - file system or the application using the device is distributed and cloud aware. Their wrong usage might cause data corruption. Audit: Passes when no VirtualMachine in any namespace has a disk with shareable set to true (needs jq). Requires oc logged in to the cluster with read access.
reference: CIS Red Hat OpenShift Virtual Machine Extension Benchmark v1.0.0 - 3.2 Disable Shareable disks

audit.command: command -v oc >/dev/null 2>&1 || exit 1; command -v jq >/dev/null 2>&1 || exit 1; out=$(oc get vm -A -o json) || exit 1; printf '%s' "$out" | jq -e '[.items[]|select(.spec.template.spec.domain.devices.disks[]?.shareable == true)]|length == 0' >/dev/null && echo compliant || echo noncompliant

remediation.command: Remove the shareable flag from any diskwhere it is found. For example, to remove the shareable flag on the first disk (index 0) of a given VM, this command can be used: $ oc patch vm <vm-name> --type='json' -p='[ {"op": "remove", "path": "/spec/template/spec/domain/devices/disks/0/shareable"}, ]' To set a shareable flag to false on every disk, this (experimental) command can be used: $ oc get vm <vm - name> - o json | jq '.spec.template.spec.domain.devices.disks[] += {"shareable":false}' | oc apply -f -

title: Ensure errorPolicy is not set to ignore
description: Error policies for disks control how Input/Output (IO) errors are handled. If a read or write operation fails on the storage, an IO error occurs. Setting the error policy to ignore is not recommended because it makes it difficult to determine the root cause of any IO issues, which can lead to data loss if the data is not correctly written to the disk. The benchmark marks this recommendation Manual; TMAegis reports it as a manual review item with the audit steps.
reference: CIS Red Hat OpenShift Virtual Machine Extension Benchmark v1.0.0 - 3.3 Ensure errorPolicy is not set to ignore

audit.command: Verify that no virtual machines are using the set to : errorPolicy ignore $ oc get vm - ojson - A | jq '.items[] | select(.spec.template.spec.domain.devices.disks[].errorPolicy == "ignore")| .metadata.namespace + "/" + .metadata.name'

remediation.command: Remove the or set it to (default value) or (suggested option errorPolicy stop report for Windows Shared Cluster Filesystem). For example, to remove the errorPolicy flag on the first disk (index 0) of a given VM, this command can be used: $ oc patch vm <vm-name> --type='json' -p='[ {"op": "remove", "path": "/spec/template/spec/domain/devices/disks/0/errorPolicy"}, ]' To set an errorPolicy flag to stop on every disk, this (experimental) command can be used: $ oc get vm <vm - name> - o json | jq '.spec.template.spec.domain.devices.disks[] += {"errorPolicy":"stop"}' | oc apply -f -

title: Use dedicated VLANs to segment network traffic
description: To ensure that virtual machines cannot access each other's network interfaces, it is crucial to segment them completely using separate VLANs. By connecting virtual machines to logically separated VLANs, you enforce network segmentation at the L2 level, preventing virtual machines from unauthorized/unintended data transmission, and reducing the risk of security breaches or data leaks. The benchmark marks this Automated, but whether VLANs are configured is a design decision per network provider, so TMAegis reports it as a manual review item with the audit commands.
reference: CIS Red Hat OpenShift Virtual Machine Extension Benchmark v1.0.0 - 4.1 Use dedicated VLANs to segment network traffic

audit.command: Use the following command to determine if VLANs are configured for OVN Kubernetes: $ oc get networkattachmentdefinition -o json | jq ".items[].spec.config" Review the output to determine if VLANs are configured correctly: config: | - { "type": "ovn - k8s - cni - overlay", "topology": "localnet", "vlanID": 100 } Please refer to the latest OpenShift documentation for more information. Use the following command to determine if VLANs are configured for SR-IOV: $ oc get sriovnetwork -o json | jq ".items[].spec.vlan" Output will return null for networks without VLANs configured, or a VLAN ID (e.g., 100 ). Please refer to the latest OpenShift documentation for more information. ...

remediation.command: Use dedicated VLANs as required. Please refer to the latest OpenShift documentation for the appropriate networking provider. Documentation:SR-IOV CNI,VLAN with bridge CNI,VLAN with OVN localnet.

title: Enable MAC spoof filtering
description: Mac spoof filtering is a feature that helps prevent man - in - the - middle attacks by verifying the authenticity of MAC addresses in network packets. By checking the MAC address of incoming packets, mac - spoof filtering can help ensure that only authorized devices are able to communicate with a particular device or network. Audit: Passes when every SR-IOV network has spoofChk "on" and every bridge-type NetworkAttachmentDefinition sets macspoofchk to true (needs jq). OVN Kubernetes localnet filters MAC spoofing by default. Requires oc logged in to the cluster with read access.
reference: CIS Red Hat OpenShift Virtual Machine Extension Benchmark v1.0.0 - 4.2 Enable MAC spoof filtering

audit.command: command -v oc >/dev/null 2>&1 || exit 1; command -v jq >/dev/null 2>&1 || exit 1; s=$(oc get sriovnetwork -A -o json 2>/dev/null || echo '{"items":[]}'); n=$(oc get network-attachment-definitions -A -o json) || exit 1; b1=$(printf '%s' "$s" | jq '[.items[]|select(.spec.spoofChk != "on")]|length'); b2=$(printf '%s' "$n" | jq '[.items[]|(.spec.config|fromjson? // {})|select(.type == "bridge")|select(.macspoofchk != true)]|length'); [ "$b1" = 0 ] && [ "$b2" = 0 ] && echo compliant || echo noncompliant

remediation.command: Enable MAC-spoof filtering per the deployed networking provider instructions. Instructions for Bridge CNI and SR-IOV CNI.

title: Disable Intel Trusted Execution Technology (TXT)
description: Intel Trusted Execution Technology (TXT) is a security - related CPU feature that is not currently leveraged by OpenShift or Openshift virtualization. The benchmark marks this recommendation Manual; TMAegis reports it as a manual review item with the audit steps.
reference: CIS Red Hat OpenShift Virtual Machine Extension Benchmark v1.0.0 - 5.1 Disable Intel Trusted Execution Technology (TXT)

audit.command: Use the following command to return the BIOS settings for a physical host: $ fwupdmgr get - bios - settings Look for , and ensure the is TxT Current value Disabled

remediation.command: Disable TXT via the firmware settings of each worker node.

title: Disable nested virtualization
description: Enabling nested virtualization in OpenShift Virtualization allows virtual machines to run within a hypervisor that is itself running on top of an existing operating system. This setup, known as nested virtualization, enables the VMs to access the full range of virtualization features provided by the underlying host, including access to the virtualization stack. In this case, Openshift Virtualization uses nested virtualization to provide its VMs with access to the entire virtualization stack, allowing them to take advantage of advanced virtualization capabilities such as live migration, resource pooling, and cloning. ... The benchmark marks this recommendation Manual; TMAegis reports it as a manual review item with the audit steps.
reference: CIS Red Hat OpenShift Virtual Machine Extension Benchmark v1.0.0 - 6.1 Disable nested virtualization

audit.command: To check the state of nested virtualization on nodes running on Intel CPUs: $ cat /sys/module/kvm_intel/parameters/nested Disabled is denoted by 0 , and enable is denoted with 1 . If you’re using AMD CPUs, replace kvm_intel with kvm_amd .

remediation.command: Add the appropriate kernel arguments to the MachineConfigPools of the workers nodes and reboot them. See https://docs.redhat.com/en/documentation/openshift_container_platform/4.18/html/instal lation _configuration/installing - customizing#installation - special - config - kargs_installing - customizing

title: Enable vCPU metrics
description: Openshift Virtualization provides metrics that you can use to monitor the consumption of cluster infrastructure resources, including vCPU. In order to use the vCPU metric, the schedstats=enable kernel argument must be applied. The benchmark marks this recommendation Manual; TMAegis reports it as a manual review item with the audit steps.
reference: CIS Red Hat OpenShift Virtual Machine Extension Benchmark v1.0.0 - 6.2 Enable vCPU metrics

audit.command: Verify if the option is enabled in the kernel command line: $ cat /proc/cmdline | grep schedstats=enable

remediation.command: Enable the kernel option on all workernodes as documented in Chapter 1. Customizing nodes | Red Hat Product Documentation

title: Ensure all CPU vulnerabilities are mitigated
description: Ensure that all known CPU vulnerabilities are mitigated. This ensures that known attacks, such as Spectre, Meltdown, etc. either do not affect the node or are mitigated via software. The benchmark marks this recommendation Manual; TMAegis reports it as a manual review item with the audit steps.
reference: CIS Red Hat OpenShift Virtual Machine Extension Benchmark v1.0.0 - 6.3 Ensure all CPU vulnerabilities are mitigated

audit.command: View CPU mitigations: $ ls /sys/devices/system/cpu/vulnerabilities Output may resemble the following: "Not affected" CPU is not affected by the vulnerability "Vulnerable" CPU is affected and no mitigation in effect "Mitigation: $M" CPU is affected and mitigation $M is in effect

remediation.command: Add the appropriate kernel arguments to the MachineConfigPools of the workers nodes and reboot them. See Documentation Chapter 1.Customizing nodes | Red Hat Product Documentation

title: Ensure KSM is disabled
description: Kernel Samepage Merging (KSM) is a Linux kernel feature that merges identical memory pages across virtual machines running on a single host, potentially reducing memory usage and improving system performance. Audit: Passes when .spec.ksmConfiguration of the HyperConverged resource is unset or false (KSM is disabled by default); any KSM node selector configuration fails. Requires oc logged in to the cluster with read access.
reference: CIS Red Hat OpenShift Virtual Machine Extension Benchmark v1.0.0 - 1.7 Ensure KSM is disabled

audit.command: command -v oc >/dev/null 2>&1 || exit 1; v=$(oc get hyperconvergeds kubevirt-hyperconverged -n openshift-cnv -o jsonpath='{.spec.ksmConfiguration}') || exit 1; case "$v" in ""|false|null|"{}") echo compliant;; *) echo noncompliant;; esac

remediation.command: Disable the KSM feature.For example, by directly editing the object with oc edit hyperconverged kubevirt-hyperconverged -n openshift-cnv and set the field to false

title: Use multi-network policies
description: Micro-segmentation in VLANs is crucial for enhancing network security because it allows control of traffic flow between different components of the network and their services. This segmentation helps to contain potential security breaches and limit the spread of malware or unauthorized access to information. The benchmark marks this recommendation Manual; TMAegis reports it as a manual review item with the audit steps.
reference: CIS Red Hat OpenShift Virtual Machine Extension Benchmark v1.0.0 - 4.3 Use multi-network policies

audit.command: By default, no MultiNetworkPolicies are defined. To segregate one or more VMs/Pods in a project, you create MultiNetworkPolicy objects in that project to indicate the allowed incoming connections on a given network. Project administrators can create and delete MultiNetworkPolicy objects within their own project. Run the following command and review the MultiNetworkPolicy objects created in the cluster. $ oc -n all get multi-networkpolicy Ensure that each namespace defined in the cluster has at least one Multi - network Policy.

remediation.command: Follow the documentation linked below and create Multi - Network Polic y objects as you need them. Note: A Multi - network Policy must match a VM and also the this VM is connected to. NetworkAttachmentDefinition
